title: One export algorithm, steps left to subclasses

blocks.text: An abstract class can provide a **common base implementation** that related classes complete. In the *template method* pattern, the abstract class owns the algorithm in one `final` method and leaves its **steps** abstract, so each subclass supplies only what differs. A *hook* is a step with a default that a subclass may override.
`Exporters.Exporter` is abstract. Write its final method

which builds, each line ending in `"\n"`: the `header()` line (only when the hook `includeHeader()` answers `true`, its default), then one line per item, `formatItem(position, item)` with the 0-based position, then the `footer()` line. Then write the three exporters:
`<n>` is the number of items exported: `footer` is given it.

new Markdown().export(["apple", "pear"]) -> "# Items
1. apple
2. pear
(2 items)
"
new Csv().export(["apple"])              -> "index,item
0,apple
end
"
new Plain().export(["apple"])            -> "apple
--
"
new Markdown().export([])                -> "# Items
(0 items)
"

cases.says: The Markdown and CSV exporters run the shared export algorithm, each with its own header, item format and footer.
Exporting no items still writes the header and the footer.
The plain exporter turns the includeHeader() hook off, and export then writes no header line.
The Markdown exporter numbers its items from 1, while the CSV exporter's index starts at 0.

concepts: An abstract class can own an algorithm in a final method and leave its steps abstract, so each subclass supplies only what differs.
